doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Brown's dissertation on Kenny Clarke and Max Roach
summary: Brown explains his Olly Wilson transcription dissertation as tape four begins.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Can you tell me about, are we on?(to Kimery) I'll just name the tape. This is tape four.
I mentioned Kenny Clarke the other day.
But my dissertation is on Kenny Clarke and Max Roach so whatever you can share coming from Detroit about "Holmes", "Klook-a-Mop"...'Cause I know Diz and Klook, and it was in Teddy Hill's band, see...
And Edgar Hayes, they go back.
So this dissertation was on two drummers?
I'll keep that in mind, it's very possible.

[laughs] And I did it with Olly Wilson. So the way Olly Wilson did it was that we had to transcribe and I know you are a stickler on transcription. He would get, he would say "Brown, here's Shaw 'Nuff. I want you to transcribe every sonic event." Not what Charlie played, not what Diz played, not the piano solo, every sonic event. So we had to do the comping, we had to get all the fills and everything on the drums...You know, bass...you had to have every sonic event captured on paper, so that's why it took me nine years to get mine. [laughs]
Olly is ill. He had a pace-maker and he had to get it replace, the first one didn't work. I talked to him just before coming down here, I'm going to meet with him on Saturday.
I will do that, I figured that you two were very close. You just had him down here in October, he talked about that.
